overall: The AG found the Wayland School Committee violated G.L. c. 39, §23B by vague executive session purposes (including 'personnel'), skipping roll call votes before executive session, and inaccurately recording those votes in minutes; no order issued, only a recommendation to amend minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged 25 executive session purposes were too vague, including 'collective bargaining' without naming the union and 'personnel' as a reason.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to state the purpose for which the body entered executive session with sufficient specificity to inform the public of what business it was deliberating upon and failing to state a valid reason for entering executive session, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee entered executive session at 25 meetings without first taking a roll call vote of its members.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to conduct a roll call vote of the Committee and failing to accurately record the actions taken during the meeting, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 39, §23B.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the minutes wrongly recorded that roll call votes were taken before executive sessions when none were conducted.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to conduct a roll call vote of the Committee and failing to accurately record the actions taken during the meeting, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 39, §23B.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
